general_information.Description: Objectives: This course is designed to introduce students to the basic concepts of Sociolinguistics and the relationship between language and society, and how language is used in multilingual speech communities. Description: The course helps students: ~Understand sociolinguistic terminology or concepts to apply in research and real-life practices. ~Use language appropriately in different social contexts. ~Interpret the social relationships in a community, and the way people convey and construct aspects of their social identity through language. ~Examine some similarities and differences in the way people use their language to convey meaning in association with society. Teaching method: This course applies instructional, communicative, and interactive discussions with: ~instructions on lessons and exercises meant to apply learnt skills. ~researching features of sociolinguistics through presentations and project work. ~open-minded approach to questions and issues that may arise during lessons. ~lectures and seminars to enhance interest in the field of sociolinguistics.
general_information.StudentTasks: ~Students must attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination. ~Be punctual for class. ~Actively participate in class discussions. ~Preview and review the lessons. ~Check vocabulary for comprehension. ~Do the exercises before, during, and after class. ~Hand in homework and class requirements. ~Work with a group for group discussions and activities.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Demonstrate understanding of sociolinguistic theories and concepts through AI-enhanced theoretical exploration (ChatGPT, Perplexity.ai, Scite.ai)
Analyze language maintenance, language shift, and multilingualism in different communities using AI-powered research synthesis (Claude, NotebookLM)

Analyse how language varies in nations with different types of language used and how a language is planned to become a national language through AI-assisted policy analysis (Scite.ai, ChatGPT, Elicit.org)

Explain how language differs in regions in terms of accents and dialects and the influence of age and gender on language use using AI-enhanced phonetic analysis (Praat, ChatGPT, Perplexity.ai, Scite.ai)
Examine the relationship between ethnicity, social networks, and language change through AI-simulated sociolinguistic research (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity.ai)
Examine how language varies according to its style and context using computational stylistic analysis tools (Stylo, ChatGPT, Gemini)
Apply knowledge of speech functions, politeness, gender, and stereotypes in communication through AI-generated discourse analysis (Scite.ai, ChatGPT, Claude)
Explore the relationship between language, culture, and perception in cross-cultural communication using AI-enhanced comparative analysis (Claude, ChatGPT, Scite.ai)
Demonstrate teamwork and collaboration in sociolinguistic research projects through AI-supported collaborative methodologies (Miro, Notion AI, ChatGPT)
